replication.target_description: Hong Kong replication; street-cleanliness government-service experiment; regression-based path analysis, Figure 4; performance → satisfaction, direct effect. Expectations and performance are randomized binary treatments; disconfirmation is self-reported performance minus expectations; satisfaction is rated 1–7.

n.sample_role: Hong Kong participants with valid responses in the final analytic sample used for the regression-based path model
n.exclusions: Screened for living or working in the city for more than 1 year; data cleaned and incomplete responses eliminated. Attention check included; detailed exclusion breakdown not specified here.
n.location: p. 782, section 4.1; p. 785, model sample-size caption
n.quote: the final sample for analysis contained 992 valid responses from Hong Kong and 1228 from Shenzhen.

es.location: p. 786, Figure 4, Hong Kong, performance → satisfaction, direct effect; coefficient convention in p. 785 figure caption

p.location: p. 786, Figure 4, Hong Kong, performance → satisfaction, direct effect; significance legend on p. 785

reported_success.quote: We can therefore conclude that we replicated the study by Van Ryzin (2013)

notes: Original full text unavailable after publisher 403, Unpaywall/OpenAlex no OA copy, and title/DOI searches. Replication full paper title and DOI verified. Replication effect and p refer to the same Figure 4 path, not the factorial main effects in Table 1. Figure 4 significance marks use the p. 785 caption legend; the Figure 4 caption itself describes the separate factorial analysis. Author success verdict is paper-level and supported by the results statement that core relationships were significant and in the predicted direction. The original coefficients reproduced in replication Figure 1 were not substituted for primary original-paper extraction. Input study_r label is not independently numbered in the paper; city and test supplied in the neutral description identify the target.
